Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin vērus (“true”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈvero/
  • Audio 1:(file)
  • Audio 2:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ero
  • Syllabification: ve‧ro

Noun

[edit]

vero (accusative singular veron, plural veroj, accusative plural verojn)

  1. truth
    Synonym: vereco
  2. reality
    Synonyms: realeco, realaĵo, realo

Derived terms

[edit]
  • malvera (“untrue”)
  • malveraĵo (“untruth”)
  • malvero (“untruth”)
  • vera (“true”)
  • vere (“truly”)
  • vereco (“truth”)
  • verigi (“to realize”)
  • veriĝi (“to come true”)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “vero”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “vero”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-present

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Finnic *vero,[1] possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *werᴈ. Cognate to Karelian vero, and possibly Votic vero and Veps vero.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈʋero/, [ˈʋe̞ro̞]
  • Rhymes: -ero
  • Syllabification(key): ve‧ro
  • Hyphenation(key): ve‧ro

Noun

[edit]

vero

  1. tax (money paid to the government)
    maksaa veroa/veroja ― to pay a tax/taxes
    määrätä vero jollekin ― to impose a tax on something
    panna jokin verolle ― to start taxing something (literally, “to put something on tax”)
    joutua verolle ― to become taxable (literally, “to end up on tax”)
    alentaa/nostaa veroa ― to lower/raise a tax
    välttää veroja ― to avoid taxes
    kiertää veroja ― to evade taxes

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin vērus (“true”), from Proto-Italic *wēros, from a Proto-Indo-European *weh₁-ros, from *weh₁- (“true”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈve.ro/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ero
  • Hyphenation: vé‧ro

Adjective

[edit]

vero (feminine vera, masculine plural veri, feminine plural vere, superlative verissimo, adverb veramente)

  1. true
    Se non è vero, è ben trovato.
    If it is not true, it is a good story.
  2. real, genuine
    Synonyms: reale, genuino

Noun

[edit]

vero m (plural veri)

  1. truth

Related terms

[edit]
  • davvero
  • ovvero
  • verace
  • veridico
  • verificare
  • verismo
  • verità
  • veritiero
  • verosimile

Further reading

[edit]
  • vero in Treccani.it – Vocabolario Treccani on line, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana

Anagrams

[edit]
  • ervo, vore

Latin

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • viro (Merovingian)

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈweː.roː]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈvɛː.ro]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • (but): ů

Etymology 1

[edit]

From vērus +‎ -ō (adverb-forming suffix).

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • verò (early modern)

Adverb

[edit]

vērō (not comparable)

  1. verily, truly, really, doubtless, in truth, indeed
    • 63 BCE, Cicero, Catiline Orations Oratio in Catilinam Prima in Senatu Habita.14:
      Quid vērō?
      What [about it], indeed?
  2. in particular, specifically
  3. (as a postpositive) but
    • 4th century, St Jerome, Vulgate, Tobit 1:23
      Tobias vero cum filio suo et cum uxore fugiens nudus latuit quia multi diligebant eum.
      But Tobias fleeing naked away with his son and with his wife, lay concealed, for many loved him.

Etymology 2

[edit]

From vērus +‎ -ō (verb-forming suffix).

Verb

[edit]

vērō (present infinitive vērāre, perfect active vērāvī, supine vērātum); first conjugation, no passive

  1. (archaic) to tell the truth
    • Ennius, Annales, quoted by Aulus Gellius, Noctes Atticae, XVIII, 16:
      satin vates verant aetate in agunda?
